text: Education Layer 1 universe should be ranked around infrastructure and capacity nodes: online program operating stack, healthcare licensure capacity, workforce training, K-12 virtual learning, student-loan/payment systems, credential/testing trust, and student lifecycle software.

The strongest underfollowed public-market angle remains supplier infrastructure behind institutions and employers: university services, student lifecycle systems, education payments, clinical simulation, credentialing/testing, and learning management workflows.

LOPE, NNI, and COUR currently rank as the most relevant initial research candidates because they map most directly to fixed-cost online education infrastructure, student lifecycle/payment systems, and university/employer platform distribution.

Several candidates beyond the visible Layer 1B evidence are retained only as hypotheses and need current filing verification before surviving Layer 2, especially D2L.TO, IEL.AX, UDMY, STRA, PRDO, APEI, GHC, WLY, CHGG, NRDY, and BNED.

Layer 2 should add a live market screen for market cap, liquidity, analyst coverage, short interest, valuation, revenue growth, segment purity, and regulatory exposure across US, Canada, UK, and Australia listings.

Healthcare education bottleneck research should explicitly search for public suppliers in nursing simulation, clinical-placement management, licensure exam prep, proctoring, lab equipment, VR simulation, and state authorization workflows.

Education theme should be decomposed into demand nodes, operating infrastructure, regulated capacity, distribution workflows, and credential trust rather than only online-learning apps or school operators.
Highest-priority bottleneck candidate: accreditation/Title IV/gainful-employment/student-outcome compliance, because demand is not monetizable without regulatory eligibility and acceptable outcomes.
Healthcare licensure and clinical-training capacity appears to be a strong bottleneck node; verify clinical placement limits, simulation substitution, lab/site capacity, and ABSN/OTA growth.

Course-material distribution and inclusive-access programs may hide bottleneck value through embedded relationships among campuses, publishers, tuition/fee billing, financial aid, and student access workflows.

University-services/OPM-like infrastructure is potentially chokepoint-like when it combines enrollment marketing, counseling, student support, compliance review, technology, and long-dated university contracts.
Nelnet-like payment, servicing, and institutional workflow systems should be treated as a hidden education-infrastructure node rather than screened only as financial services.
Hybrid/asynchronous delivery model proof points are catalysts only if they improve capacity utilization without degrading graduation, placement, retention, or compliance outcomes.
Employer-funded workforce training partnerships are a watch item because they could shift the buyer from individual learners to recurring enterprise procurement budgets.

Need primary-source verification for each candidate's revenue mix, segment margins, customer concentration, contract duration, regulatory exposure, student outcomes, and renewal rates before Layer 2B ranking.
Need direct filings or company materials to verify CAE healthcare simulation education exposure; current support is speculative and should not be upgraded without revenue/backlog/customer evidence.
Consumer AI learning apps should be ranked below regulated/embedded infrastructure unless evidence shows institutional adoption, credential trust, or durable enterprise/school procurement.

LOPE should remain the highest-priority relationship in this candidate chunk: it is directly mapped to university-services operating infrastructure, online/hybrid program scale, student lifecycle support, and healthcare education expansion.
NNI should remain in the underfollowed lane but requires immediate filing verification because the education infrastructure thesis may be obscured by student-loan and financial-services labeling.
COUR maps to platform and credential distribution, but should not be upgraded until degree economics, enterprise retention, campus renewals, and AI-driven content competition are verified.

ATGE and LRN are better treated as reference demand anchors than pure underfollowed suppliers; their value is in revealing healthcare licensure, clinical-placement, online delivery, K-12 funding, and career-learning demand signals.
CAE remains a speculative shadow supplier; upgrade only if healthcare simulation revenue, education customers, backlog, or clinical-training bottleneck linkage is material in current disclosures.
WNC should not be treated as an education supplier; retain only as a weak employer-training demand read-through unless named vendor relationships or material training spend are documented.

PSO and DUOL are high-attention reference benchmarks for assessment, credentialing, consumer learning, and AI learning; they should not crowd out underfollowed infrastructure candidates in later layers.

Need current market caps, analyst coverage, liquidity, segment revenue, customer concentration, and valuation-pricing checks for LOPE, NNI, COUR, ATGE, LRN, CAE, WNC, PSO, and DUOL before Layer 3 ranking.

Need direct source verification from latest filings for NNI, COUR, ATGE, LRN, CAE, WNC, PSO, and DUOL because current relationship mapping relies mainly on cached candidate context and inference rather than fresh primary evidence.

GHC should remain in the Education funnel as an underfollowed diversified-holdco/Kaplan exposure, but it cannot be upgraded until Kaplan segment revenue, margin, and value contribution are verified from filings.
CHGG should be treated primarily as a speculative shadow/negative-control ticker for consumer study-help demand under AI disruption rather than as a clean bottleneck candidate.
WLY maps to academic publishing, research content, and education-content workflows; next layer should verify whether education/institutional content exposure is material and growing.
UDMY maps to enterprise workforce training if enterprise ARR, retention, and customer count offset consumer marketplace weakness; verify enterprise mix and net retention before upgrading.

D2L.TO is the cleanest institutional software/workflow candidate in this chunk by node fit, but evidence remains filing-dependent: ARR, retention, margin, customer concentration, and LMS competitive position are required.
IEL.AX maps to international student mobility, language testing, and university placement infrastructure, with policy and visa exposure as both catalyst and risk.
NRDY should stay only as a clearly labeled speculative micro-cap AI tutoring/live-learning unit-economics test case; liquidity and cash runway are gating evidence.

BNED has the strongest external evidence in this chunk for an education-procurement/workflow relationship through First Day and campus course materials, but micro-cap balance-sheet/refinancing risk may dominate theme exposure.

Need current public market data for GHC, CHGG, WLY, UDMY, D2L.TO, IEL.AX, NRDY, and BNED: market cap, liquidity, short interest, analyst coverage, institutional ownership, debt maturity, and valuation to complete pricing checks.

Need primary-source filings for all eight tickers in this chunk; most ticker relationships outside BNED are currently hypotheses derived from Layer 1 candidate mapping rather than independently verified current facts.
